text: The device hums. Evening by a river in the hills east of the Jordan. Tents, flocks and children everywhere.
Twenty years have passed. Jacob worked for his uncle Laban in Haran, married Leah and Rachel, and has eleven sons now. God told him it was time to go home.

speaker: The LORD
text: Go back to the land of your fathers and to your kindred, and I will be with you.

speaker: Jacob
text: Esau... what will he do, {name}?

speaker: Jacob
text: My hip aches, {name}. But I would not trade last night for anything.
When the messengers returned to Jacob, they said, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is coming to meet you—he and four hundred men with him.”
In great fear and distress, Jacob divided his people into two camps, as well as the flocks and herds and camels.

speaker: Jacob
text: Four hundred men, {name}! Twenty years ago my brother wanted to kill me. I have to pray.

speaker: Jacob
text: I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness You have shown Your servant. Indeed, with only my staff I came across the Jordan, but now I have become two camps. Please deliver me from the hand of my brother Esau, for I am afraid that he may come and attack me and the mothers and children with me. But You have said, ‘I will surely make you prosper, and I will make your offspring like the sand of the sea, too numerous to count.’
Jacob was afraid, and he told God so. He did not pretend he deserved help. He held on to what God had promised.

speaker: Jacob
text: I will send gifts ahead to my brother, herd after herd. Help the drover at the ford, {name}. Bring him the goats, the camels and the donkeys, one herd at a time.
Fine, healthy animals.
One herd at a time.
The herd follows you. Take it to the drover at the ford.
Off they go across the ford, toward Esau.

speaker: Drover
text: That's a lot of animals to give away.

speaker: Drover
text: Bring me a herd, and I'll send it across.

Jacob spent the night there, and from what he had brought with him, he selected a gift for his brother Esau: 200 female goats, 20 male goats, 200 ewes, 20 rams, 30 milk camels with their young, 40 cows, 10 bulls, 20 female donkeys, and 10 male donkeys.
… For he thought, “I will appease Esau with the gift that is going before me. After that I can face him, and perhaps he will accept me.”
During the night Jacob got up and took his two wives, his two maidservants, and his eleven sons, and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.

speaker: Jacob
text: Go across with them, {name}. I will stay here a while.

speaker: Rachel
text: Stay close to Joseph, {name}. He is only small.

speaker: Maidservant
text: So many children to keep track of!

speaker: Jacob's son
text: Is Uncle Esau really bringing four hundred men?
So Jacob was left all alone, and there a man wrestled with him until daybreak.
When the man saw that he could not overpower Jacob, he struck the socket of Jacob’s hip and dislocated it as they wrestled.

speaker: The man
text: Let me go, for it is daybreak.

speaker: Jacob
text: I will not let you go unless you bless me.

speaker: The man
text: What is your name?

speaker: Jacob
text: Jacob,

speaker: The man
text: Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with men, and you have prevailed.
Israel means "he struggles with God."
Jacob had always got ahead by tricks. This time he held on to God and would not let go without a blessing. God gave him a new name.

speaker: Jacob
text: Please tell me your name.

speaker: The man
text: Why do you ask my name?
… Then he blessed Jacob there.
So Jacob named the place Peniel, saying, “Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared.”
Peniel means "face of God."
The sun rose above him as he passed by Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip.

Now Jacob looked up and saw Esau coming toward him with four hundred men. So he divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two maidservants. He put the maidservants and their children in front, Leah and her children next, and Rachel and Joseph at the rear.
But Jacob himself went on ahead and bowed to the ground seven times as he approached his brother.
Esau, however, ran to him and embraced him, threw his arms around his neck, and kissed him. And they both wept.
Twenty years of fear, and Esau ran to him with open arms. Forgiveness did what all the gifts could not.
Long after, Jesus told a story about a son who came home after wasting everything. Listen to how his father welcomed him:

speaker: Jesus
text: … But while he was still in the distance, his father saw him and was filled with compassion. He ran to his son, embraced him, and kissed him.
That is how God welcomes everyone who comes home to Him.

speaker: Esau
text: Who are these with you?

speaker: Jacob
text: These are the children God has graciously given your servant.

speaker: Esau
text: What do you mean by sending this whole company to meet me?

speaker: Jacob
text: To find favor in your sight, my lord,

speaker: Esau
text: I already have plenty, my brother, | Keep what belongs to you.

speaker: Jacob
text: No, please! If I have found favor in your sight, then receive this gift from my hand. For indeed, I have seen your face, and it is like seeing the face of God, since you have received me favorably.

speaker: Esau
text: Where is my brother?

speaker: Esau
text: My brother! After all these years.

speaker: Esau's man
text: Esau told us to wait here.

speaker: Jacob
text: Last night God gave me a new name, and this morning He gave me back my brother. Everything He promised me at Bethel, He has done, {name}.
Esau goes home to Seir. Jacob, now called Israel, travels on into Canaan with all his family. Your device hums. Time to go.

speaker: Messenger
text: On the road here, Jacob says, angels came to meet him!
Jacob also went on his way, and the angels of God met him. When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is the camp of God.” So he named that place Mahanaim.

speaker: Herdsman
text: Two hundred female goats, twenty males, two hundred ewes, twenty rams, thirty camels, fifty cattle, thirty donkeys... five hundred and fifty animals, not counting the baby camels! All of it earned in twenty hard years with Laban.

speaker: Jacob
text: Thus for twenty years I have served in your household—fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flocks—and you have changed my wages ten times!

speaker: Leah
text: This is my fourth son, Judah. When he was born, I said: this time I will praise the LORD.
And once more she conceived and gave birth to a son and said, “This time I will praise the LORD.” So she named him Judah. …
Long after, King David was born into Judah's family, and so was Jesus:
Abraham was the father of Isaac, Isaac the father of Jacob, and Jacob the father of Judah and his brothers.

speaker: Joseph
text: I'm Joseph! I'm the youngest. Mother says God gave me to her.
She named him Joseph, and said, “May the LORD add to me another son.”
Joseph will grow up to have a story all of his own.

speaker: Esau's man
text: We came ready for a fight. And look at those two!
A letter, written long after:
Be kind and tenderhearted to one another, forgiving each other just as in Christ God forgave you.
The glowing door nearby leads back to your time device.
Your discoveries are saved. When you come back, the story picks up from this part.

Esau, however, ran to him and embraced him, threw his arms around his neck, and kissed him. And they both wept.
Jacob came home afraid of what he deserved, and found forgiveness instead. That is the welcome God offers every one of us through Jesus.
Twenty years after he fled, Jacob came home. Hearing that Esau was coming with 400 men, he was afraid, and he prayed. (32:1-12)
He sent herds ahead as a gift for his brother. (32:13-21)
At night by the Jabbok a man wrestled with Jacob until daybreak and gave him a new name: Israel. (32:22-32)
Jacob bowed seven times, but Esau ran to him, embraced him and kissed him, and they wept. (33:1-11)
Esau went home to Seir, and Jacob went on into Canaan. (33:12-20)
You, and that you led the herds to the drover.
The drover, the messenger, the herdsman and Esau's men, and what Jacob's family said to you. Only two of Jacob's eleven sons are shown.
What the man who wrestled Jacob looked like. The Bible calls him a man; Jacob said he had seen God face to face (32:30), and Hosea 12:4 calls him an angel.
Genesis 29-31: Jacob's twenty years with Laban, who tricked him into marrying Leah before Rachel, and how Jacob's family grew.
Genesis 34 tells of a terrible wrong done to Jacob's daughter Dinah and her brothers' violent revenge. It is best read with a parent.
Genesis 35: at Bethel God called Jacob Israel again; Benjamin was born, and Rachel died.
